passages.subject: Taurus: Facula
passages.excerpt: one of the Hyades which is bright and ruddy, and called Facula, has the same temperament as Mars
passages.notes: Footnote marker omitted. Printed footnote identifies Facula as Aldebaran.

passages.author: Ptolemy
passages.locator: Book I, chapter IX, printed p. 25, Gemini: Apollo and Hercules; PDF page 58
passages.subject: Gemini: Apollo and Hercules
passages.excerpt: the one, which precedes and is called Apollo, is like Mercury; the other which follows, called Hercules, is like Mars.
passages.notes: Footnote markers omitted. Footnotes identify Apollo as Castor and Hercules as Pollux. This interpretation describes Apollo only; Hercules has Mars, not Mercury.

passages.author: Ptolemy
passages.locator: Book I, chapter IX, printed p. 26, Leo: Regulus; PDF page 59
passages.subject: Leo: Regulus
passages.excerpt: The bright one in the heart, called Regulus, agrees with Mars and Jupiter.
passages.notes: Footnote marker omitted. Footnote gives Cor Leonis.

passages.author: Ptolemy
passages.locator: Book I, chapter IX, printed p. 26, Virgo: Vindemiator; PDF page 59
passages.subject: Virgo: Vindemiator
passages.excerpt: The bright one in the northern wing, called Vindemiator, is of the same influence as Saturn and Mercury

passages.author: Ptolemy

passages.subject: Virgo: Spica Virginis

passages.subject: Scorpio: three stars in the body including Antares
passages.excerpt: the three in the body itself, the middle one of which, called Antares, is ruddy and more luminous, are similar to Mars and moderately to Jupiter
passages.notes: Footnote marker omitted. The attribution covers a group with Antares explicitly named.

passages.subject: Ursa Minor

passages.subject: Orion: shoulders and other bright stars
passages.excerpt: The stars on the shoulders operate similarly to Mars and Mercury; and the other bright stars to Jupiter and Saturn.
passages.notes: Interpretation describes shoulder stars only; other bright stars have Jupiter and Saturn.

passages.notes: Interpretation describes the bright mouth star only; other stars have Venus. The passage does not name Sirius.
